claimChecks.claim: FMCSA Military Skills Test Waiver can waive the CDL road/skills test for qualified military drivers
claimChecks.detail: Waives the skills (driving) test only, NOT the knowledge test. Eligibility: currently licensed and employed within the past 12 months in a military position requiring operation of a vehicle equivalent to a CMV, with ~2 years' safe experience and no disqualifying violations in the prior 2 years; available in every state. The separate Even Exchange Program (FMCSA-endorsed) waives the knowledge test for qualifying military occupations in participating states; combined, a military license can be exchanged for a CDL with no tests. Changes: on July 15, 2026 the President announced automatic CDL eligibility for military heavy-truck drivers; per Transport Topics, FMCSA updated the Even Exchange page that day to list qualifying MOSs (e.g., Army 88M), but no final rule has been issued. A Feb 19, 2026 Federal Register CDL document on the military-personnel exception exists but could not be read (redirect block). No official source mentions a 'SummitCDL' program - treat that name as unverified. Copy suggestion: add the 12-month window and note the knowledge test still applies unless the state participates in Even Exchange. NOTE: fmcsa.dot.gov returned 403 on both URL attempts; findings are from fmcsa.dot.gov WebSearch snippets.

claimChecks.claim: Documented military maintenance experience can authorize testing for the FAA A&P certificate
claimChecks.detail: 14 CFR 65.77 requires either an aviation maintenance technician school graduation document or 'documentary evidence, satisfactory to the Administrator, of practical experience' - at least 18 months for one rating or 30 months concurrent for both airframe and powerplant. FAA guidance: practical experience from U.S. military aviation maintenance occupations may be evaluated by the FAA for authorization to take the mechanic knowledge test; holders of a JSAMTCC Certificate of Eligibility are considered to have met 65.77 for the rating(s) on the COE and need no additional FAA authorization to begin testing. Applicant must still pass knowledge, oral and practical tests. NOTE: faa.gov returned 403 and ecfr.gov redirected to a bot block; findings are from faa.gov/fsims.faa.gov WebSearch snippets (FAA Order 8900.1 Vol 5 Ch 5) and the 65.77 text.

claimChecks.claim: Helmets to Hardhats places veterans into union apprenticeships
claimChecks.detail: H2H is a free national program, operated under contract with the Center for Military Recruitment, Assessment and Veterans' Employment, that connects National Guard, Reserve, retired and transitioning service members with union building-trades careers and registered apprenticeships ('We Connect Veterans with Careers'). It is a connector/referral path, not the hiring body: admission is decided by the local union/JATC apprenticeship program, though some DOL-registered union apprenticeship standards (e.g., IUPAT sample standards) provide entry for H2H participants who meet minimum qualifications. Suggested wording: 'connects veterans to union apprenticeships' rather than 'places'. No DOL page describing H2H itself was found; the DOL reference is a WebSearch snippet of the IUPAT sample standards PDF.

claimChecks.claim: SDVOSB set-aside contracts exist; SBA VetCert is the certification path
claimChecks.detail: SBA: 'Certification with SBA allows service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses (SDVOSBs) to compete for federal sole-source and set-aside contracts' across the federal government; certified VOSBs get additional set-aside/sole-source opportunities at VA; for VA 'There is no self-certification provision.' Certification moved from VA to SBA on Jan 1, 2023 (NDAA FY2021), and since Jan 1, 2024 SBA certification (or a pending application filed by Dec 31, 2023) is required for SDVOSB sole-source/set-aside awards governmentwide; uncertified firms may only self-represent for awards outside the SDVOSB program. Application portal per SBA page: https://certifications.sba.gov/ (VetCert).
